title: Updated Assessment on Impact on Singapore's Economy and Businesses from New 15% Tariffs
what_it_is: Updated Assessment on Impact on Singapore's Economy and Businesses from New 15% Tariffs

sections.label: US section 122 tariff
sections.summary: The US imposed a 10% tariff under section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, collected from 24 February 2026, with limited expected impact on Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: On the same day, the US announced a tariff of 10% under section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 on all US imports for 150 days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The US Customs and Border Protection started collecting this 10% tariff from 12.01 am on 24 February 2026, US time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The immediate direct impact of these tariff developments on Singapore's economy is not expected to be significant, given that the current section 122 tariff of 10% is broadly unchanged from the previous 10% "reciprocal" tariff that had been imposed on Singapore's exports to the US since April 2025.

sections.label: BizAdapt support levels raised
sections.summary: At Budget 2026, the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance announced BizAdapt support levels would be raised from up to 50% to up to 70%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: At Budget 2026, the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance announced that support levels under BizAdapt would be raised from up to 50%, to up to 70%.

sections.label: Tariff impact on Singapore
sections.summary: The tariffs' impact on Singapore's economy has been assessed as rather limited thus far.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Just let me highlight that thus far, the tariffs' impact on Singapore's economy, we have assessed it to be rather limited.

sections.label: SBF playbook for companies
sections.summary: SBF published a playbook guiding companies on risk-mapping, re-configuring supply chains, and digitalising and innovating, with further measures ready when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: For example, SBF has published a playbook to guide companies on key actions to take, such as how to sense-make the impact through risk-mapping, to take action, such as re-configuring their supply chains, and also planning ahead by digitalising and innovating to build long-term resilience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We stand ready to roll out further measures to support sectors that are affected, when necessary.

sections.label: Safeguarding and expanding economic space
sections.summary: Singapore will safeguard and expand its economic space by deepening, diversifying and defending economic interests and trade linkages, including with emerging markets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: I actually suggest that she refer to my speech in the Ministry of Trade and Industry's (MTI's) Committee of Supply (COS).

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: But just to highlight a few key points, Singapore will continue to safeguard and expand our economic space by deepening, diversifying and also defending our economic interest, and also our trade linkages with all our trading partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In addition to strengthening trade links with key trading partners, we are also pursuing closer trade relations with emerging markets, such as Latin America, South Asia, Middle East and Africa, and also furthering our cooperation in growth areas through digital and green economy agreements, such as the EU-Singapore Digital Trade Agreement.
